questions.question: This patient developed prosthetic valve endocarditis caused by Enterococcus faecalis 3 months after his TAV-in-TAV procedure. What is the recommended antimicrobial treatment regimen for enterococcal prosthetic valve endocarditis, and what key differences exist compared to native valve endocarditis in terms of duration and agent selection?

In a TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV procedure, the risk of coronary artery obstruction is a critical concern due to multiple overlapping stent frames and leaflet material. What specific CT-derived measurements are used to assess coronary obstruction risk, and what is the significance of the 'neo-skirt' concept in procedural planning?

Immediately after the third TAVI, this patient had a mean gradient of 67 mm Hg, an indexed aortic valve area of 0.4 cm²/m², and a Doppler velocity index of 0.24—consistent with severe prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM). How is PPM defined and graded using indexed effective orifice area, and what are the major clinical consequences of severe PPM after transcatheter valve implantation?

This patient presented with progressive dyspnea, exertional chest discomfort, dizziness, and fatigue 2 years after his second TAVI, with echocardiography showing a mean gradient of 49 mm Hg and an aortic valve area of 0.5 cm². What are the main mechanisms of structural valve deterioration in transcatheter bioprostheses, and how did the prior episode of infective endocarditis likely contribute to the degeneration process in this case?

The procedural team deliberately employed a high implantation strategy for the third transcatheter valve, positioning it at the level of the Evolut valve leaflets. What is the rationale for this high implantation approach in terms of effective orifice area preservation, coronary flow maintenance, and prevention of leaflet folding, and what are the potential trade-offs of this strategy?

According to the 2025 ESC guidelines for the management of valvular heart disease and infective endocarditis, what is the recommended treatment strategy for prosthetic valve endocarditis, and under what circumstances might a transcatheter approach be considered instead of surgery in a patient with prior TAVI who develops PVE?

One month after the third TAVI, the mean transvalvular gradient decreased dramatically from 67 mm Hg to 27 mm Hg without any additional intervention. What mechanisms explain this delayed improvement in gradient, including the role of balloon post-dilation on the prior Evolut frame, commissural alignment, and frame remodeling over time?

If the third transcatheter prosthesis in this patient were to fail prematurely, treatment options would be extremely limited. What is the BASILICA (bioprosthetic or native aortic scallop intentional laceration to prevent iatrogenic coronary artery obstruction) technique, and what are the theoretical advantages and limitations of this approach in a triple-stented aortic valve configuration?

The Acurate neo2 prosthesis was specifically selected for this third TAVI. What design characteristics of the Acurate neo2—such as supra-annular leaflet positioning, frame height, and commissural alignment features—make it suitable for implantation within a narrow anatomy containing two prior transcatheter valve frames, and how do these features compare to those of other self-expanding valves like the Evolut?
